text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Palestinian Authority: Accelerated talks in exchange for settlement freeze.
- Police consider questioning top Netanyahu aide Avigdor Lieberman in connection with Gregory Lerner investigation.
- U.S. administration bars American companies from maintaining commercial ties with Ben Gurion university, suspecting the institution of involvement in nuclear development.
- Ultra-orthodox Jews assaulted Conservative movement Jews, Palestinians and police in Jerusalem.
- 350 children in Gaza hospitalised with meningitis. Israeli Health Ministry: Little chance disease will spread to Israel.
- Egytpian envoy Osama al-Baz to meet Netanyahu, Arafat today.
- Building contractor discovered calf's severed head in his car; police think it was a mafia warning directed at the wrong man.
- Defence Minister appointed commission to look into permits given for quarrying in West Bank.
- U.S. will not launch initiative to break Israel-PLO impasse.
